# Image Filtering and Acquisition for Detection Damage of Conveyor Belts

Paweł Maślak1

(1)

Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, Wrocław University of Technology, 50-370 Wrocław, Poland

Paweł Maślak

Email: pawel.maslak@pwr.edu.pl

Abstract

Recently, a large growth may be observed in the field of usage of machine vision in various types of industry. The aim of that article is to show the possibilities of using the machine vision in mining industry for detecting damage in conveyor belt caused by the various types of factors. In the article it is presented the test stand on which the test were conducted, the aim of filtering, selected filtered image, image acquisition and the conclusion.

Keywords

Image acquisitionImage filteringBelt conveyors

## 1 Introduction

A digital image is modelled using function f of two variables indicated mostly due x, y. Both the field and set the functions of the digital image are discreet. Points of the image function f assigns values corresponding to the colours, the most common are the three colours R—red, G—green and B—blue—RGB. Image description is available in many references [3, 4, 8–10]. The same value image function is defined as the brightness, but often the image may represent other physical quantities, e.g. Temperature and degree of radiation penetration. The image that takes only two possible values is a binary image. If the values are the various shades of gray, it is a monochrome image [1–7, 10].

## 2 Test Stand

Laboratory measurements were performed on a piece of rubber belt with steel cord with the typical damages the surface and with a prepared slit. A camera SICK Ranger C55 with software Ranger Studio was used for the measurements. Figure 1 shows a scheme of positions Camera-Laser used to laboratory measurements of camera SICK Ranger C55 and illuminator laser of power 50 mW [6].

The test stand allows to set the camera at any angle alpha in the range of 0–90° and setting the illuminator at an angle beta to the same extent. In the measurements were carried out for three types of settings:

  * Ordinary: α = 0°, β > 0°

  * Reversed ordinary: α > 0°, β = 0°

  * Specular: α > 0°, β > 0°

In the Fig. 2 it is shown the view of test stand. The camera and the laser illumination are on the one plane perpendicular to the surface. The test stand allows to set the camera and the laser at any level between 0 and 500 mm.

## 3 Image Filtering

Filtration is a mathematical operation on the pixels of the source image, the result of which is obtained a new, transformed image. Filtration is defined as the transformation of the context, as to determine the new value of the target pixel of the image information is needed from many pixels of the source image.

The use of filters in image processing means that the new value points are taken into account the points with his surroundings. Each pixel of the environment contributes to—weight during the calculations. These weights are stored in the form of masks. Typical sizes mask is 3 × 3, 5 × 5 or 7 × 7 size masks are usually odd, since the pixel in the center represents the pixel for which the operation is performed transform filter. Filtration analyzed on the basis of the mask filter h 3 × 3 in the image L [8, 9, 11]:

Filtration was carried out separately for each component of the image. So if we have an image represented in RGB, then we will perform a separate transform for component R, G and B. An attempt to use filtration for the points located on the edge of the image, leading to a situation in which the mask "extends" beyond the processed image. There are several ways to work around this problem. One of them is the omission of the filtration process to close, the other is to reduce the image after filtration of the points for which the process can not be executed. Another way is to add to the filtered image pixels located in duplicate on the edge.

In image filtering there are typical filters used for images [8, 9, 11]:

  * Gauss filter,

  * Robert's filter,

  * Prewitt's filters,

  * Sobel's filters,

  * Kirsch's filters,

  * Laplace's filters,

  * Mediana's filters.

For detecting damages in belt conveyors images the best are the Laplace's filters. The usage of that filter is shown on Fig. 3.

Due to the lack of directionality it turned out to be the best filtering Laplace operators. This type of filter is used in subsequent steps to prepare the image or scan for further analysis.

## 4 Image Acquisition

On the selected piece of the belt tests were conducted including checking the minimum exposure time to obtain images and scan of sufficient quality for further analysis. As a measure of quality was the percentage of the number of points with the value "0". The value of "0" does not give the information needed to determine the profile of the scan. The fewer points the better the quality of the scan. The measurements were carried out for 5 settings of camera-laser according to Table 1.

Table 1

Set no. |   |   | Exposure time (μs)

---|---|---|---

I | 45 | 0 | 500 ÷ 2500

II | 30 | 0 | 500 ÷ 2500

III | 0 | 30 | 500 ÷ 2500

IV | 0 | 45 | 500 ÷ 3000

V | 30 | 30 | 500 ÷ 2500

The best results were found for set V then for II. For exposure time 1300 μs there were 2.46% for V set and 3.08% of "0" for set II. The figure shown at Fig. 7 shows the result of the algorithm for the analysis of collected images and scans of the analyzed segment of the belt.

## 5 Summary

The selected method for filtering and image acquisition are necessary for next steps which are processing and image analysis. The results of the image analysis can be used in automatic belt conveyors monitoring systems. Those systems should be in common use, because they would be reliable and could avoid human presence in dangerous environment. The dust and high humidity cause the very hard conditions for a human and make problems to identify the eventual damage of belt. Monitoring system always measures with the same precision at any time and any conditions. Monitoring system works 24 h a day, 7 days a week and let the industry work well. It is possible to create the system, that works in real time conditions.

# Analysis of the Blood Flow Through the Centrifugal Pump

Joanna Mikołajczak1  , Jakub Słowiński1 and Maciej Zawiślak1

(1)

University of Technology, Wrocław, Poland

Joanna Mikołajczak (Corresponding author)

Email: joanna.mikolajczak89@gmail.com

Maciej Zawiślak

Email: maciej.zawislak@pwr.edu.pl

Abstract

Blood flow simulation was conducted for the peripheral centrifugal pump of the artificial heart by use of numerical methods. Flow parameters were examined for the destruction of blood morphological elements, the results were compared with literature data. The learned lessons led to changes of the pump geometry, then further simulations for different constructional variants were carried out. The results of calculations led to choosing the best structural solution for heart pump and follow-on conclusions on what kind of changes may improve the flow parameters and reduce the risk of destruction of blood elements.

## 1 Introduction

Basic problems that appear during designing artificial heart or heart assist are: formation of blood clots and processes of blood elements destruction. In the heart pumps, clot formation may appear in areas of increased shear stress, local blood stagnation as well as in contact with the elements of low bio-compatibility [1]. However, haemolysis is a process of Red Blood Cells (RBC) destruction, during which an excessive deformation of the erythrocytes takes place which ultimately leads to the release of haemoglobin to plasma. The primary factors responsible for the initiation and the scale of damage are such as: shear stress rate (acceptable values are 150–500 Pa [1–5]) and the time of exposure of RBC to stress [1].

Modern blood pumps are designed to prevent the rapid destruction of RBC. However, there is a need to minimize the deformation of RBC's so that it does not lead to the rapid destruction but to gradual, irreversible changes instead. This leads to i.e. haemoglobin release to plasma and thus deterioration of patient's condition through the RBC aggregation, filtration of which by kidneys causes dysfunction of them as well as other organs [1]. The task of the heart pump is therefore to ensure proper blood flow and to cause minimal impact on destruction of blood elements. The aim of this study was to perform numerical simulation of blood flow through centrifugal pump and then to make the attempt to improve the flow and minimize the process of blood elements destruction.

## 2 Material

The peripheral centrifugal pump of artificial heart, which replaces the work done by the left ventricle was studied. A 3-D model of the artificial heart centrifugal pump was developed based on the technical documentation of the artificial heart project obtained from the Department of Biomedical Engineering and Experimental Mechanics, Institute of Machine Design and Operation Wrocław University of Technology, Poland. The basic dimensions of pump are presented in the Table 1.

Table 1

Basic dimensions of pump

Parameter | Description | Value (mm)

---|---|---

  | Chamber diameter | 114

  | Housing diameter | 132

H | Pump height | 27

## 3 Method

Numerical calculations of blood flow through the centrifugal pump were performed in ANSYS Fluent and ANSYS Workbench. Tetra4 and Hexa8 elements (for the volume directly in contact with rotor) were selected for discretization. The assumed blood density was 1050 kg/m3, whereas the viscosity was 3.5 * 10-3 Pa * s [1, 6–8]. Selected turbulence model was: k-ε.

In order to model blood flow through the centrifugal pumps, MRF (eng. Multi Reference Frame) method was used which requires the allotment of the rotation zone, the stationary flow zone and the boundary surfaces. These interfaces make transmission of information between the zones possible. The stationary flow zone was created with inlet, outlet and side channels while for the rotating zone, the volumes were assumed directly coming into contact with the walls of rotor, which were given the rotor rotational speed of 450 rev/min.

Analyzed different pump designs

---

I and III top housing design

II and IV top housing design

I and III rotor design | II and IV rotor design

  |

Staright blades (90° angle) | Slanted blades (110° angle)

The modeled pump simulates the blood flow from pulmonary veins into the right ventricle of the heart. The flow rate for the heart ventricle is Q = 5 l/min [1, 6, 8]. The speed of blood at the mouth of the pulmonary vein is 0.26 m/s while the pressure is 5–7 mmHg. The pressure occurring at the outlet of aorta is 13.3 kPa [1]. According to the work parameters of the designed pump the deformation of the left ventricle is 725.8 Pa. Hence, the pump pressure for the left ventricle is 14.03 kPa. An additional parameter was the turbulence intensity which according to the literature is 3% [8].

## 4 Results

### 4.1 The Analysis of the Blood Flow Through the Pump

The calculations done on the base geometry made it possible to create a model of blood flow through the artificial heart peripheral centrifugal pump. The pressure distribution similar to the physiological one was obtained (Fig. 1). The velocity distribution shows a significant increase of the fluid velocity at the exit from the side channel to the discharge port and the maximum velocity of 3.4 m/s at the inlet-side channels connector. The formation of such velocities and the turbulence presence in this area affect adversely blood elements. The critical shear stress value of 350 Pa occurs is the pump impeller (Fig. 2). According to the literature, this value is too high and causes the RBC destruction. Haemolysis does not occur when the stress value is lower than 150 Pa.

### 4.2 The Analysis of the Blood Flow for Different Variants of the Pump Geometry

The next step of the study was to simulate the blood flow in the four variants of the pump geometry in order to improve flow characteristics. The results are presented in the Table 2.

### 4.3 FSI—Fluid Structural Interaction

The third stage of the study was the structural analysis of the rotor, conducted using FSI (Fluid Structural Interaction) method, which allows one to link flow simulation with structure strength analysis. In the structural analysis One-Way FSI was used—a method that allows obtaining similar-to-actual input data for the structural analysis out of the output data of the flow analysis. Rotor geometries were used as geometrical model for the stress analysis: base (straight blades) and adjusted (slanted blades) made of titanium. The changes in pressure caused by the flow were used for strength-of-the-structure calculations.

The obtained stress values of the impeller blades caused by the blood flow are small (maximum value of 0.28 MPa) and do not affect the strength of the structure in any way. The stress distribution is similar in two variations of the rotor geometry.

## 5 Summary of the Results

The simulation of the blood flow through the artificial heart centrifugal pump made it possible to analyze the conditions prevailing in the pump and showed the velocity and pressure distribution in it. The calculations showed that it was necessary to improve the flow conditions i.e. the reduction of the maximum flow rate, the reduction of the areas where zero or close to zero velocities occurred, the reduction of turbulence in the pump spigots and reduction of shear stress which leads to haemolysis.

Therefore, the studies of the flow for the redesigned geometries of the pump housing and the rotor were performed and the results are presented in Table 2. The analysis of the tested flow parameters for all designs are as follows:

  * The change of the geometry of the suction inlet and the discharge port resulted in the reduction of the maximum velocities in the pump chamber and a significant pressure reduction on the rotor,

  * The change of the rotor in the base geometry of the pump caused a significant reduction in velocity and shear stress values to non-destructive of RBC

  * The simultaneous change in the geometry of the pump chamber and the rotor did not cause the aggregation of the good results that were observed individually.

The case studies led us to the conclusion that the improvement in the inlet and outlet geometry is necessary in order to reduce the turbulence in the critical areas. Whereas, the causes of the destruction of the blood elements can be seen in the rotor geometry. Large liquid velocities and shear stress were reduced by changing the angle of the blades. These changes, in both analyzed cases, improve the situation (reduction maximum velocity of blood and also reduction the maximum shear stress by half). It can therefore be concluded, that angle of the blades is the decisive parameter that determinates the flow correctness.

## 6 Conclusion

The adjustment implemented to the pump geometry, examination and analysis resulted in reducing the vortex forming in channels, the significant reduction of maximum velocities (to the non-destructive for RBC), reducing near-zero velocities which further reduces the risk of blood stagnation and the blood clots, reducing shear stress significantly which causes the haemolysis.

The obtained results show the direction in which the blood pump design can develop—the change of the blade angle and rotor geometry in order to minimize the shear stress. This seems to be the decisive aspect for the possibilities of using the pump in the system supporting heart work or replacing it completely.

# Topology Optimization of Structures Subjected to Transient Thermomechanical Loading

Mirosław W. Mrzygłód1  and Piotr Duda2

(1)

Department of Mechanics and Machine Design, Opole University of Technology, Ul. Mikołajczyka 5, 45-271 Opole, Poland

(2)

Institute of Thermal Power Engineering, Cracow University of Technology, Al. Jana Pawła II 37, 31-864 Kraków, Poland

Mirosław W. Mrzygłód (Corresponding author)

Email: m.mrzyglod@po.opole.pl

Piotr Duda

Email: pduda@mech.pk.edu.pl

Abstract

A new methodology for layout optimization of structures, which are subjected to transient thermo-mechanical loads, is presented. In the investigation, an evolutionary algorithm of topology optimization is used. For the purpose of the thermomechanical analysis, a new method of cumulative damage summation of the full thermo-mechanical time load history is considered. Moreover, to obtain an easy-to-manufacture shape, a new procedure for the layering reduction of unnecessary material is proposed. The proposed methodology is illustrated in the example of design optimization of a power block device. In the optimization process, the constraints of the maximum total stress in the whole cycle are assumed. As the basis of transient load regime, the TRD 301 regulations are used.

## 1 Introduction

The development of CAD/CAE tools allows to constantly increase a field of their application to the analysis and optimization of newly designed structures. Topology optimization is one of the fastest growing methods of finding preliminary design solutions in advanced industries [1]. The majority of available in the literature examples of thermomechanical structural optimization refer to the steady state load conditions. However, the examples of structures optimization in a variable or cyclic thermomechanical load conditions are very rare. Yoon et al. [2] use isogeometric analysis to solve the heat conduction equation and compute shape design sensitivity coefficients. The topology optimization methodology has been applied to this type of problem. Bruggi and Cinquini [3], under the steady-state assumption, address the problem of the optimal design of thermal insulation in building engineering. They use numerical implementation of topology optimization based on the heat conduction equation. Anflora et al. [4] employ the topological optimization procedure to heat transfer problems considering anisotropy and multiple regions.

In this work, a new method of topology optimization of structures subjected to transient thermomechanical loading will be proposed. In the investigation, the constant criterion surface algorithm (CCSA) of topology optimization will be used. The algorithm will be enriched with new procedures of imposing manufacturing constraints and cumulative damage summation of the full thermo-mechanical time load history.

## 2 The Algorithm of Topology Optimization

The CCSA algorithm for solving the thermo-mechanical problems is formulated as follows:

(1)

the constraints are:

(2)

where:   represent constraints, e.g. equivalent stress;   are the upper bounds of the constraints and f (α i ) is the objective function (the volume of the structure).

The algorithm consists of a procedure of iterative elimination of low-stressed elements controlled by the volume percentage reduction constant ΔF [5]. To find the ΔF value, a constraint criterion limit g min is dynamically calculated at every iteration. In the case of crossing the limit, the CCSA algorithm adds a layer of finite elements to the entire boundary of the structure. The process of increasing the volume of the structure is continued until the constraint g returns to admissible values. By increasing and decreasing the structure's volume, the algorithm improves the solution. After completion of the predetermined maximum number of iterations L MX , the program saves the best solution in the form of a vector of design variables α i * [5].

To take into account multi-step time load history, a modified 'compare and save maximum' procedure of cumulative summation of constraint criterion values is proposed. The method assumes that during each iteration, for every finite element the values of the constraint measure of all M load steps are compared to those previously written to the equivalent design space. After the comparison, only the highest values of the current and former are stored in the equivalent design space. The final cumulative matrix of the constraint criterion is used by the CCSA algorithm of topology optimization.

Moreover, to obtain an easy-to-manufacture shape, a new procedure for the layering reduction of unnecessary material is proposed. Procedure allows not only to control the amount subtracted materials (ΔF), but also keeps an intelligent control on the spot of the removal. Figure 1 shows how procedure selecting only a part of the area of the external layer of the design space.

Fig. 1

Intelligent control procedure of the material removal: example of design space (marked in blue) (a), the removing the portion of the outer layer by the procedure (b)

## 3 The Example of Structural Optimization

As an example of optimization of a typical structure of T-pipe is selected. T-pipe is the part of pre-heated steam pipelines in a power unit of a 360 MW power plant. It was designed for the pressure pin = 18 MPa and steam temperature Tw = 540 °C. Its weight equals 1378 kg. The geometry of the T-pipe is presented in Fig. 2a.

Fig. 2

Geometry (a) and FE model (b) of the T-pipe structure

T-pipe was made out of an alloy steel 14 MoV63 (13 HMF). This steel has a high yield strength, Re = 206 MPa at the temperature T = 500 °C. Thermal and mechanical properties are shown in Fig. 3 [6].

Fig. 3

Thermal (a) and mechanical (b) properties for the steel 14 MoV63 (13 HMF)

One fourth of the T-pipe was divided into eight-node finite brick elements based on the symmetry conditions. It is shown in Fig. 2b. Time-space temperature and stress distribution in T-pipe are calculated using ANSYS software [7].

Temperature distribution in time and space is calculated assuming that the heat transfer coefficient on the inner surfaces of T-pipe equals 1000 W/m2 K [8, 10]. Next, stress analyses are carried out. The stress model is constrained to ensure symmetry conditions. It allows for the possibility of free lengthening in the direction of the horizontal and vertical pipe. Additionally, the surfaces connecting the T-pipe with the pipeline must be planes and calculated temperature distribution in space and time is used as a body load in the stress model. As the base of transient load regime, the TRD 301 regulations are used [9] (see Fig. 4). In the optimization process, the constraints of the maximum Huber-Mises-Hencky (HMH) equivalent stress in the whole cycle are assumed.

Fig. 4

The calculated medium temperature and medium pressure according to TRD 301

The structure is subjected to topology optimization. T-pipe reinforcement on the outer surfaces of the structure is considered as the design space and is shown in Fig. 2b. Based on the design space a new vector of design variables vectors of temperature dependent material properties of each finite element of the design space. The optimization 'speed' of CCSA algorithm was set at the level of 0.006% volume percentage reduction ΔF. The searching history of optimal layout of the structure is presented in Fig. 5a. In Fig. 5b–c, the result of optimization is shown. The volume of optimal solution consists of 93% of starting volume.

Fig. 5

History of searching for a solution (a) and the best solution (b, c)

## 4 Conclusions

A new methodology for layout optimization of structures, which are subjected to transient thermo-mechanical loads, is presented.

In the investigation, the CCSA algorithm of topology optimization is used. For the purpose of the thermomechanical analysis, a new method of cumulative damage summation of the full thermomechanical time load history is considered. To obtain an easy-to-manufacture shape, a new procedure for the layering reduction of unnecessary material is proposed.

The methodology is illustrated by the example of structure optimization of T-pipe with transient load regime according to the TRD 301 regulations. Thanks to the application of the manufacturing constraints, the optimum layout of the structure do not require a high financial outlay.

# Investigation of Influence of Unevenly Spaced Blades onto Working Parameters of Centrifugal Fans Impellers Used in Mine Ventilation

Piotr Odyjas1  , Przemysław Moczko1, Maciej Zawiślak1 and Damian Pietrusiak1

(1)

Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, Department of Machine Design and Research, Wrocław University of Science and Technology, Wrocław, Poland

Piotr Odyjas

Email: piotr.odyjas@pwr.edu.pl

Abstract

Centrifugal fans are widely used in order to move air or other gases in ducts. As exact as possible manufacturing of fan is required in order to ensure long time of operation and desired flow parameters. In the article evaluation of influence of unevenly spaced blades onto flow parameters of impeller is considered. Thanks to usage of numerical simulation, few different configuration of blades inaccuracies could be compared with basic ideal case. Received results suggests that inaccuracies in circumferential blade spacing influences flow pattern across impeller and changes flow parameters of fan. It is interesting that in few cases efficiency of impeller is higher than in basic solution, but in fact such situation cannot been accepted since in these cases non-uniform fluid force distribution can cause higher vibrations of fan. In general, differences of efficiency are small what suggests that influence of unevenly spaced blades onto flow parameters can be in many cases neglected.

## 1 Introduction

Proper operation of fans depends strongly on manufacturing quality of its components. These influence fans working parameters as well as their durability [1–6]. As showed experiences of fans manufacturer in Poland, high-grade work influences not only fans vibration, but also their flow parameters and as result efficiency and power consumption of fan. Impellers are basic centrifugal fans components that ensure change of the mechanical energy onto hydraulic energy [1–4, 7, 8]. In case of fans used in main mine ventilation systems, sizes of the impellers are often huge. That results in strong instability effects during fan working due to any mass imbalance. Because of that each impeller needs to be statically and dynamically balanced [4–6]. Such approach ensures longer time of operation of fans components.

As showed literature survey, there are not any scientific works subjected onto investigation of inaccuracies in fans components manufacturing, onto their working parameters, especially efficiency as well as power consumption and pressure ratio. As mentioned, with accordance with experience of centrifugal fans manufacturers in Poland and companies using centrifugal fans, inaccuracies in fan manufacturing influences not only vibration of fans but also their flow parameters. Due to that fact, authors decided to check influence of unevenly spaced centrifugal fans blades onto fan's impeller operational parameters. Tool used to investigation this influence was numerical simulations of planar centrifugal impeller models in few configurations. Application of planar model in centrifugal fans impellers optimization process seems to be a very useful tool, since such models are not complex and ensure fast comparison of many models [8, 9]. All simulations have been done onto one of the centrifugal fans impellers used in main ventilation systems in Polish mines. Basic parameters describing this impeller are showed in Table 1.

Table 1

## 2 Configuration of Impeller's Blades Used During Studies

As mentioned in previous section, impeller being a subject of this work, consist of 9 blades. In order to evaluate influence of unevenly spaced blades, few configurations of circumferentially spaced blades have been prepared:

  1. (1)

Configuration A—basic configuration in which impellers blades are evenly spaced what corresponds to case of ideally manufactured impeller.

  2. (2)

Configuration B—configuration of fan blades in which each consecutive blade is circumferentially shifted about 0.25° less what results in widening blade passages.

  3. (3)

Configuration C—configuration of fan blades in which each consecutive blade is circumferentially shifted about 0.25° more what results in narrowing blade passages.

  4. (4)

Configuration D—configuration of fan blades in which each consecutive blade is circumferentially shifted about 1° less what results in widening blade passages.

  5. (5)

Configuration E—configuration of fan blades in which each consecutive blade is circumferentially shifted about 1° more what results in narrowing blade passages.

  6. (6)

Configuration F—configuration of fan blades in each odd blade is circumferentially shifted about 41° instead of 40°.

  7. (7)

Configuration G—configuration of fan blades in each odd blade is circumferentially shifted about 39° instead of 40°.

All of these blades configurations beyond basic solution are showed in Fig. 1. These configurations are not exactly measured onto real impeller but are exemplary inaccuracies that can occur during impeller manufacturing and that can show tendency of changes of impeller working parameters.

Fig. 1

Configurations of unevenly spaced blades used during simulations

## 3 Numerical Model

Numerical simulations of fan are widely used tool during fans designing and optimization process [8–11]. Three dimensional as well as two dimensional procedures are used in order to evaluate fans performance. One of the most popular method of fan performance evaluation is so called frozen rotor approach, which ensures fast evaluation of steady states values [12, 13].

Each model used during numerical simulations within this work was a planar model. Unstructured mesh was used as mesh scheme during numerical model preparation. Size of mesh in each case was similar. In order to improve accuracy, boundary layer built from quadrilateral elements aimed at y += 30 has been prepared around each blade. Preliminary investigations of mesh size and used turbulence model have been prepared in order to improve accuracy of calculations. Thanks to such approach, basic size of mesh as 5 mm and turbulence model k-ϖ (SST) have been chosen. In order to reduce calculation domain, only impeller domain has been calculated. In case of model in configuration A, periodic conditions have been used since each blade is circumferentially evenly spaced. In other cases, whole impeller domain has been modeled. Exemplary meshed domain is presented onto Fig. 2.

Fig. 2

Example of meshed blade passage

In order to ensure similar numerical simulations errors, not only similarly meshed models have been calculated but also any model had the same boundary conditions. As the inlet boundary condition, velocity inlet formulation has been implemented and on the outlet of impeller pressure outlet has been chosen. Inlet velocity was defined as 20.8 m/s what gave flow rate equal to 175 m3/s. Static pressure on the outlet has been chosen equal to 0 since, each impeller has been calculated without volute.

## 4 Results of Simulation

As mentioned, any simulation has been conducted with use of the same turbulence model, the same boundary conditions and similar meshes. Thanks to received results, few basic parameters used to compare each impeller's configuration have been chosen. These parameters were total pressure rise of impeller (ΔPT) and torque on the shaft (M). Knowing rotational velocity of the impeller as well as flow rate through impeller, it was possible to calculate hydraulic and mechanical power and as result efficiency:

Received calculations results give some information about behavior of impeller with different blade configurations. In any cases, parameters calculated thanks to simulation are similar. What is more, efficiencies are similar in each case, but some interesting observation can be done. In case of two configurations (C and E), efficiency of impeller is higher, in one case is the same (F) and in other cases is smaller. Both configurations with higher efficiency of impeller are in fact similar. In both cases vane passage is wider that in basic solution and only last passage between last and first blades is narrower. The question is, if this increase of efficiency results from these wider passages or one narrower passage. Definitely pressure as well as velocity contours in both cases are similar and differ from contours in other cases.

## 5 Conclusions

Presented article aimed at finding answer for question, what is an influence of unevenly spaced blades (due to inaccuracies in impeller manufacturing) onto flow parameters of centrifugal fan's impeller. Flow parameters considered within this work were total pressure rise, mechanical and hydraulic power as well as efficiency of impeller. On this basis and thanks to conducted simulations, main conclusion has to be stated as follows: inaccuracies in circumferential distribution of blades have some influence onto impellers flow parameters.

According to received results two configurations ensure rise in impeller efficiency. In other cases efficiency is equal or lower than in case of ideally manufactured impeller. It is important to notice that in both cases with increased efficiency (configurations C and E), most of the blade passages are wider as in basic solution. In these cases it is difficult to evaluate reasons of efficiency increase. Since it is known that similar impellers equipped with 10 instead of 9 blades ensures higher efficiency, it seems that great deal of contribution onto this efficiencies increase has the narrowest blade passage which ensures better flow pattern in this region as well as higher pressure rise. In other cases, where most of the blade passages are narrower, small efficiency drop is observed. It is perhaps due to presence in these cases one definitely wider passage that does not ensure proper flow in this region. In case of configuration F, there is no difference in efficiency value, but this case differs from others since there is no very narrow and wide passages.

Ultimately it must be stated, that these results are going to be validated using experiments in nearest future. What is more, 3D models are going to be used in order to check these results since flow is definitely spacial and blade passages are narrowing in meridional plane as well. Moreover, it seems that behavior of considered within this work impellers, can differ in case when also scroll housing would be included in simulations.

# Computer Supporting of Determining Decision Interactive Variables for the Importance Rank of Construction and Exploitation Parameters Illustrated with an Example of a Gear Pump After Tooth Root Undercutting

Marian A. Partyka1  and Agnieszka Tiszbierek1

(1)

Opole, Poland

Marian A. Partyka

Email: a.deptula@po.opole.pl

Agnieszka Tiszbierek (Corresponding author)

Email: a.tiszbierek@po.opole.pl

Abstract

A gear pump after tooth root undercutting is a device, on the operation of which the following parameters have an influence.

## 1 Description of the Gear Pump After Tooth Root Undercutting Construction and the Way of Logical Encoding of Parameter Values

A gear pump after tooth root undercutting is a device, on the operation of which the following parameters have an influence:

  * n (rpm)—rotational speed,

  * M (Nm)—the torque of hydraulic and mechanical losses,

  * Q (l/min)—actual displacement;

  * P (MPa)—operating pressure.

The above-mentioned statement results from the construction of the analysed device, the prototype of which was designed, tested and produced by the hydraulic pumps manufacturing company Wytwórnia Pomp Hydraulicznych seated in Wrocław. The novelty concerning this prototype was a modification of the upper part of the profile evolvent by means of the so-called tooth. The pump construction is based on the structure of three plates (Fig. 1). The front plate (1) is used for the pump mounting in the drive device. The central plate (2) includes gear wheels, sleeve bearings of the housing and sucking, thanks to which it drives the hydraulic system connecting holes. The whole construction is closed by means of the rear plate (3) [1–7].

Fig. 1

The construction scheme of the three-plate pump

The values of parameters, presented in different chapters of this paper, are actual values taken during the process of carrying out the analyses in the proper workstation composed of the following elements: analysed pump (1), direct current motor (2), supply pump (3), alternating current motor (4), suction filter (5), shut-off valve (6), safety valves (7, 8), throttle valves (9–11), in line filter (12), vacuum meter (13, 14), manometer (15), flow meter with micro-ammeter (16), measurement microphones (17), acoustic chamber (18), tank (19), electronic speed control (20), torque sensor with a recorder (21), photocell with a counting meter (22) [1–7].

The analysed device, due to its construction and work process, has three kinds of efficiency: complete efficiency (η c ); volumetric efficiency (η v ) as well as hydraulic - mechanical efficiency (η hm ). This fact caused the division of the search for the optimal set of construction and exploitation parameters into three groups of analyses divided on the basis of the analysed efficiency. In addition, in order to limit the scope of analyses, the following arithmetic values of changes scopes for given efficiencies were adopted according to the following scheme: η v ≥ 0.96; η hm ≥ 0.89; η c ≥ 0.86. The obtained actual values of construction and exploitation parameters had to be properly encoded and selected depending on the analysed pump efficiency. The way of encoding and the scope of values included in the scope of a given encoded value are presented in Tables 1 and 2.

Properly chosen and ordered values of particular parameters made it possible to carry out further analyses of the determination process of their importance rank. The method of logical multi-valued trees was the method of determining optimal sets. Results obtained in this way made it possible to notice dependencies existing among particular parameters, resulting from their properties. Parameters M and pt as well as the parameters n and Qrz form two groups of parameters depending on each other, the interaction of which has an unquestionable influence on the operation of the analysed device. This is why, the idea of creating substitute variables for particular groups of parameters in the scope of particular efficiencies appeared.

The calculations were made by means of a computer programme [8], which encoded the substitute variable by itself and then showed particular optimal sets.

## 2 Computer—Assisted Calculations of the Set of Parameters with the Application of the Substitute Value

When the properly prepared data was entered into the computer programme, it was necessary to indicate values included in the substitute variable and then start the calculating process. It was necessary to carry out calculations for each of the analysed efficiencies separately, enter only those lines which met the criterion indicated for a given efficiency and encode the substitute variable separately. Separate calculations are required due to the existing properties of each efficiency, which cause rejection or choosing a subsequent line from the table of data. As it has been mentioned earlier, the programme encoded each substitute variable by itself and the way of encoding is presented in Table 3. It is necessary to notice that due to the data selection and non-continuity of the data occurrence, the encoded value of the substitute variable (e.g. the "0" value) is composed of another set of substitute values for each efficiency. It results from the fact that there are other sets inside the substitute variable for particular efficiencies.

On the basis of the obtained results (both the indirect calculations and the optimal sets), it is possible to state that the substitute variable should always be located in the upper part of the logical multi-valued tree, what is turn means that its importance rank is lower than that of the remaining ones.

In addition, it is possible to notice that the remaining parameters obtain the same value of the importance rank, thus the theory about two groups of parameters depending on each other is confirmed. Therefore, it is possible to consider the introduction of even two variables.

Examples of optimal logical multi-valued trees for a chosen efficiency are presented in Fig. 3. The branches in bold represent appearing parameter values, inserted in the programme in an appropriate sequence (Fig. 4).

Examples of multi-valued logical trees presenting optimal sets of parameters (an example for the complete pump efficiency as well as the hydraulic and mechanical pump efficiency with the substitute variable z   (pM))

## 3 Conclusions

Computer-assisted calculations confirmed the dependence of parameters Q and n as well as p and M, also showing a similar importance of each importance rank for the analysed variables. The lower value of the importance rank of the substitute variable undoubtedly results from the fact of connecting two parameters as well as from rejecting, in the calculations, a group of data which did not meet the criterion set for each efficiency. This rejection had unquestionable influence on the encoding process of the substitute variable, its valency and it, in turn, had an influence on the reduction process in the computer-assisted calculations. Undoubtedly, its application prevented from dividing interactive parameters and limited the number of possible combinations of parameters occurrence, what in turn shortened the whole calculation process. If the method of logical trees was used in the analysed case, without inserting the substitute variable, it would be necessary to draw as many as twenty-four combinations of parameter sets and then, choose optimal ones among them (for each efficiency separately, obviously).

The analysed calculation process and specifications resulting from the properties of each actual object, which is the gear pump after tooth root undercutting, make it possible to draw interesting conclusions on the optimization of such devices, contributing to their better and more effective operation.

# Application of Piezoelectric Films for Measuring Dynamical Response of Freight Wagons During Exploitation

Marek Płaczek1  , Andrzej Wróbel1  and Andrzej Buchacz1

(1)

Silesian University of Technology, Konarskiego 18A, 44-100 Gliwice, Poland

Marek Płaczek (Corresponding author)

Email: marek.placzek@polsl.pl

Andrzej Wróbel

Email: andrzej.wrobel@polsl.pl

Abstract

This paper contains a report on the research of possibilities of the use of piezoelectric transducers in the form of composite films Macro Fiber Composite (MFC) to measure the dynamic response of freight wagons type EAOS during operation. The aim of the study is to verify the possibility to develop a system of supervision of the technical condition of freight wagons, based on measurements of their dynamic response to the standard forces generated during their operation. It was assumed that the MFC piezoelectric films, due to a number of advantages can be used as sensors in the proposed measurement system and to verify the effectiveness of their operation the sequence of tests on real objects during observed rides were carried out. The repeatability of received waveforms of electric voltage, generated by the piezoelectric transducers glued on selected items of wagon stand was verified. In addition, a preliminary analysis of the received signals was done in order to determine their usefulness in the system of supervision of the technical condition of freight cars.

## 1 Introduction

The article describes the continuation of works related to the modernization of wagons implemented within the consortium formed by the scientific unit and industrial plants, which assumptions were presented in [1, 2, 14, 17]. The aim of the project is to extend the operating time between repairs of freight cars, as well as to improve their performance properties. The premise of the project is the use of composite panels, mounted on the hull of the body, during its periodic repair. The project also aims to develop a system of supervision of the technical condition of wagons and monitoring of their operating parameters in real time using the GPS system and developed system for measurement and control mounted on modernized wagons [12]. As the sensors composite piezoelectric MFC transducers were proposed, which has been tested in the series of observed, operating rides, conducted in different weather conditions [20]. The effectiveness, as well as the reproducibility of measurement signals were verified. In the further investigation an analysis of the possibility of inference about technical condition of the wagon based on the received measurement signals will be conducted.

The project is carried out by the consortium that consists of the scientific entity—the Institute of Engineering Processes Automation and Integrated Manufacturing Systems from the Silesian University of Technology and enterprises—DB Schenker Rail Poland and Germaz. The aim of this research project is to modernize the analysed wagon during its renovation using new materials. Effects that are to be achieved by the modernization are:

  * better corrosion protection of the wagon elements,

  * easier unloading of the wagon in winter conditions (no freezing of the cargo to the sides and floor of the wagon),

  * reduction of the weight of the wagon while its load increases,

  * easier management of freight cars during exploitation.

Nowadays, engineers have the opportunity to apply new materials and new methodology to design devices and systems that, for example are more effective, have better properties and lower costs of production. This is why a lot of effort is spent on development of any types of devices that are used by a human because new materials, technologies and methods are opening brand new possibilities before designers and engineers [3, 8, 10, 15]. The new opportunities are also results of the possibility of smart materials application, so the materials that can change one or more of their properties during operations and this change can be controlled [5, 13]. Smart materials are piezoelectric transducers which are widely used in many kinds of technical devices and number of their applications is still increasing.

Railway transport is very important for the development of the modern economy this is why many research works concerning with problems occurring in this way of transport and its development are being carried out all the time [2, 4, 7, 11]. The goal of those works are usually to develop the infrastructure that is used for transport of goods and people, make it more cost-effective, safe and less burden-some for the environment [9, 16, 18, 19]. Application of the composite panels to the freight wagon's body shell was proposed as the solution that can solve mentioned problems during exploitation of freight wagons in presented research work [2, 14, 17]. The composite panels composed of fiberglass and epoxy resin were proposed. They will be mounted on the body shell using rivet nuts. What is more the body shell of the modernized freight wagon will be painted using an anti-corrosion agent. Composite panels mounted on the modernized freight wagon's doors and walls are presented in Fig. 1. Glass-epoxy composites based on epoxy resin belong to the group of chemically hardenable materials. They are the result of fiberglass saturation and compressed into a layer. This type of composite is distinguished by the following features: very good mechanical properties and insulation, high parameter bending strength and compressive strength with low weight, wide range of applications, low water absorption [1, 2, 17].

Fig. 1

The composite panels mounted on the modernized freight wagon's doors and wall

On the other hand, the system for structural health monitoring should be developed as a system that includes elements from different science areas, such as mechanics, electronics and informatics. Such connection brings new possibilities and new effects, so these systems can be called a mechatronic system [5, 6, 10, 13].

## 2 MFC Piezoelectric Transducers Application in Freight Wagons

The object of research is the four axial freight wagon of ordinary type EAOS 1415-A3 production BREC Belgium. It was being taken into consideration because it is one of the most popular types of wagons designed to unload with the use of tipplers. Two EAOS freight wagons on which measurements were carried out are presented in Fig. 2. One of them was after the full regeneration of the body shell while the body shell of the second one was not repaired after a few years of exploitation. Measurements were carried out while the train was driving (locomotive and two wagons) with the maximum travelling speed about 10 km/h. The train was driving a section of about 400 m, stopped and then it was returning. The test was repeated five times to verify the repeatability of the results. Measurements were made in repair facility of DB Schenker Rail Poland in Rybnik three times in different weather conditions.

Fig. 2

Freight wagons on which measurements were carried out (series EAOS, type 1415 A3)

Measurements were carried out using analogue input cards and portable device NI cDAQ-9191—the compact 1-Slot chassis which allows Send data to a host PC over Ethernet or IEEE 802.11 Wi-Fi.

## 3 Results of Measurements

Measurement points on the freight wagons were selected as:

  * Channel 1—the centre of the top envelope of the box, interior of the freight wagon;

  * Channel 2—the support frame—the bottom surface of the main, outer beam of the frame;

  * Channel 3—the support frame—the inner surface of the main, outer beam of the frame;

  * Channel 4—the support frame—side surface of the crossbeam.

In Figs. 3 and 4 examples of results of measurements obtained for the described channels are presented. The measured profile of electric voltage generated by MFC transducer as a result of excitation occurring during operation for empty wagon and maximal speed 10 km/h for selected measuring points are presented.

Fig. 3

The measured profile of electric voltage generated by MFC transducer occurring during freight wagon operation a and results of its FFT analysis b—measuring channel 1

Fig. 4

The measured profile of electric voltage generated by MFC transducer occurring during freight wagon operation a and results of its FFT analysis b—measuring channel 4

During all measurements it could be observed that obtained results are repeatable (taking into account range of possible measurement errors) for all tested measuring points without influence of the weather conditions and temperature. It can be concluded that Macro Fiber Composite piezoelectric transducers proposed as sensors in developed system could be successfully used. They have a lot of advantages which causes that they can be proposed as a very good solution, for example they can be easily applied to the structure by gluing it to its surface. They are produced in the form of thin foils, so they also can be easily laminated into the structure of the composite panels that will be mounted in the modernized freight wagons. What is more they being resistant to weather conditions and do not require additional power source.

## 4 Discussion and Conclusions

The presented results of the carried out measurements n real objects using MFC piezoelectric foils allows to conclude that their application in the system designed for freight wagons structural health monitoring should be a good solution. As it was mentioned they can be easily applying to both, elements of a standard freight wagon as well as laminated in the composite structures of modernized wagons. They are resistant to weather conditions and do not require additional power source. What is more they can be also used as electric voltage generators in energy harvesting systems and generate electricity from the vibration of the structure [20].

In the next stage of the research project analysis of the measured signals will be carried out in order to infer about technical condition of the freight wagon's elements, especially about condition of the implemented composite panels. The measured signals should also allow detecting if the wagon is loaded and inform about that using GPS system. It will improve the management of a fleet of wagons and recording the process of their operation and its influence on technical condition of the wagon.

The measured profile of freight wagon's elements vibrations can be used in laboratory tests on models of freight wagons prepared in scale. Measurements on real objects are time consuming and generate high costs. In laboratory conditions it is easy to modify technical condition of the model and verify influence of this modification onto its dynamical response for excitations with the same parameters as those that occur during standard exploitation of freight wagons. Therefore, carried out tests were very important taking into account future research. At this moment it was impossible to do measurements on loaded and unloaded freight wagons driving with maximum speed. Those measurements should be done in the future works.

# FEM (Finite Element Method) Numeric Analyses of the Syrenka S201 Car Model

Krzysztof Podkowski1  , Zbigniew Barszcz1  and Jarosław Seńko1

(1)

Warsaw, Poland

Krzysztof Podkowski (Corresponding author)

Email: k.podkowski@pimot.eu

Zbigniew Barszcz (Corresponding author)

Email: z.barszcz@pimot.eu

Jarosław Seńko (Corresponding author)

Email: jsenko@simr.pw.edu.pl

Abstract

This presentation demonstrates the results of numerical analyses of the Syrenka S201 vehicle design. The basic strength calculations were conducted using the finite elements method (FEM) within the scope of the linear static procedure.

## 1 Introduction

This presentation demonstrates the results of numerical analyses of the Syrenka S201 vehicle design (Fig. 1). The basic strength calculations were conducted using the finite elements method (FEM) within the scope of the linear static procedure. The calculations were based on the vehicle's CAD model, material data and on the assumed exploitation loads of the vehicle. The strength calculations were conducted in the MSC.FEA (MSC.Patran + MSC.Nastran) application.

Fig. 1

Prototype picture

The purpose of the conducted numerical analysis was to capture the critical points in the structure (stress accumulation locations), nature of deformations and to determine the vehicle frame's approximate torsion stiffness.

The results of approval tests conducted in the Automotive Industry Institute are currently used as a basis to conduct the validation of numerical models and their potential modification, which would allow verifying the applied validation procedures.

Analyses were carried out under the project: "Reloaded Polish automotive industry—the implementation of a passenger vehicle—/Syrenka/", NCBR, contract No. UOD-DEM-1-529/001.

## 2 Scope of Work

The scope of work embraced the following points:

  * Analysis of the developed engineering and construction documentation of the Syrenka S201 passenger vehicle;

  * Development of the vehicle's calculation models based on the obtained 3D model of the vehicle (Fig. 2);

  * Determination of the load schematics resulting from the analysis of forces created during the vehicle's motion;

  * Initial numerical calculations of the vehicle frame's strength using the FEM for various set variants of structural loads and calculations of the frame's torsion stiffness;

  * Analysis of the results of the frame structure's strength calculations;

  * Further numerical calculations including conclusions and design changes resulting from the analysis of the initial strength calculations;

  * Final study with full description of the calculation model and the adopted assumptions, including the analysis of the obtained results from the vehicle structure's strength calculations;

  * Initial validation of the numerical models.

Fig. 2

View of the vehicle—CAD model

## 3 Vehicle Calculation Model

During the vehicle modelling, we used the general characteristics established on real objects which included elements proposed for assembly in the constructed vehicle prototype.

The basic elements of the vehicle as a mechanical system include: frame, motor with a drive unit and the drive assembly in the form of 4 drive wheels with the front suspension in the form of a shock absorber and spring as well as a rear trailing arm.

## 4 FEM Numerical Analysis—Strength Calculations (MSC.Patran/MSC.Nastran)

The analysis was prepared in the MSC.FEA (MSC.Patran + MSC.Nastran) application [1, 2]. We adopted a surface grid model—rectangular and triangular elements (locally). The average element edge length for the grid in the chassis frame amounted to 7 mm. The grid is compacted locally. Elements with significant mass were modelled as mass elements and connected with the structure using "dummy" type beam elements (Figs. 3 and 4).

Fig. 3

View of the vehicle design's calculation model developed in the MSC.Patran application

Fig. 4

View of the vehicle design's calculation model developed in the MSC.Patran application

The calculations regard the static tests for various, complex structural loads. The specified force values are the assumed values correlated with the vehicle's mass and coefficients resulting from the load schematics adopted for the calculations. The analysed structure has undergone the application of maximum, complex, predicted force values in the scope of the linear analysis for the given material—resilient structure analysis. The specified anchoring points were analogous to the equivalent chassis mounting points [3, 4].

The analysis demonstrated in the enclosed presentation is a static strength analysis of the previous version of the Syrenka's design, based on a CAD geometric model.

## 5 Example of Results (Load—Vertical Direction, Gravity—10 g)

Figures 5, 6 and 7.

Fig. 5

FEM model (load—vertical direction, gravity—10 g)

Fig. 6

Reduced stresses (MPa)

Fig. 7

Resultant deformations (mm)

## 6 Summary and Conclusions

The values of particular parameters adopted for vehicle modelling allowed us to develop its calculation model with a maximum reflection of reality. The implementation of these parameters into the FEM [1, 2, 5] application enabled us to conduct the vehicle structure's strength calculations with the adopted coercions from the ground. The obtained results of the strength calculations demonstrated the structure regions that have to be especially taken into consideration during the exploitation tests.

The purpose of the conducted numerical analysis was to capture the critical points in the structure (stress accumulation locations), determine the nature of deformations and estimate the vehicle frame's approximate torsion stiffness. In the future, the applied and positively verified validation procedures shall be applicable to the numerical analyses of other structures.

# Numerical Simulations of Composite Frontal Protection System According to EC 78/2009

Mariusz Ptak1  , Paweł Blicharski1  , Eugeniusz Rusiński1  and Jacek Karliński1

(1)

Department of Machine Design and Research, Wrocław University of Technology, Lukasiewicza 7/9, 50-371 Wroclaw, Poland

Mariusz Ptak (Corresponding author)

Email: mariusz.ptak@pwr.edu.pl

Paweł Blicharski

Email: paw.blicharski@gmail.com

Eugeniusz Rusiński

Email: eugeniusz.rusinski@pwr.edu.pl

Jacek Karliński

Email: jacek.karlinski@pwr.edu.pl

Abstract

According to Regulation (EC) 78/2009 currently in force in the European Union the frontal protection system (FPS) is a separate structure, which is intended to protect the external surface of the vehicle, from damage in the event of a collision. The use of FPS was the subject of many discussions. This was mainly due to the increasing popularity of Sport Utility Vehicles (SUV) with non-compliant bull bars fitted by owners. It should be noted that, in most cases, installing an FPS on a SUV is simply a matter of car tuning. The purpose of such modifications is to make the vehicle appear more aggressive and stand out against similar cars. The problem came when frontal protection systems became merely a fashionable decoration of sport utility vehicles in place of their original function. Unfortunately, due to their growing popularity, SUVs are increasingly involved in accidents involving pedestrians. Over the years, vehicles equipped with bull bars have been causing an increasing number of pedestrian deaths and therefore specific requirements were introduced for this component. The paper presents numerical comparison of FPS made of steel and fiberglass according to the current regulations. A notable difference in legform acceleration was noted, which indicates a good potential in fiberglass usage as a base material for FPS.

Keywords

Frontal protection system (FPS)PedestrianSafetyImpactNumerical simulationsFinite element analysis (FEA)Fiberglass

## 1 Introduction

According to police statistics in Poland in 2014 were reported 34,970 car accidents which killed 3,202 people and 42,545 were injured. In 9,106 of all crashes pedestrians took part wherein 1,127 of them were killed and 8,592 were wounded [1]. Most of all accidents took place in build-up areas but the accidents in embeddable areas were the most tragic. The reason of these all things is the speed reached in these areas. In Poland in embeddable areas the speed limit is 90 km/h but even the impact speed is about 80 km/s the chance of survival are negligible [2]. For that reason World Health Organization recommends that the speed limits in residential areas should be 30 km/h and in build-up areas should be 50 km/h [3–6]. At these speeds the chance of survival are respectively 90 and 50% [7]. On the other hand, speed is not the only cause of injury. Also the design of vehicle and additional elements have high influence on the effects of accidents. One of these kind of parts is a frontal protection system which will be further discussed below.

The FPS is an additional construction installed in vehicles mainly to protect front parts of a car like cooler, lights or body. The bull-bar was invented in Australia where car destruction caused during collisions with kangaroos are serious [8]. For that reason FPS used in Australia are massive steel structures. Over time this idea began to be used in motorsport that means vehicles which take part in off-road competitions are increasingly equipped with FPS. Thanks to that damages occurred during collisions with trees, stones and other elements of nature may be less. At some time, some people noticed that the connection FPS with chrome may improve the appearance of the car and nowadays FPS are increasingly used in this purpose.

## 2 Methodology

Due to the large impact of pedestrian safety FPS must be correctly tested according to EC 78/2009 using impactors of legs and head. In the case of impacts of leg impactor on the FPS there are measured parameters like leg acceleration, shear displacement and dynamic angle of the knee bend. To receive approvals the results of tests cannot exceed respectively: acceleration 200 g; shear displacement 6 mm; bending angle 21°. In tests with head form there is measured head performance criteria (HPC). This parameter show likelihood of the injury during impacts and its value shall not exceed 1000. There is also one additional test with upper legform but it is performed only for observation. During it the sum of the impact forces shall not exceed 7.5 kN and the bending moment on the impactor shall not exceed 510 Nm. All other conditions of tests are described in EC 78/2009 [9].

Nowadays, most of FPS are metal especially steel however composite FPS are increasingly being used. For that reason in this article there will be compared the previously mentioned two types of FPS. Steel is a typical material of construction so the choice of this material for FPS is evident (Fig. 1).

Fig. 1

Frontal protection system made of bent steel pipes, mounted on SUVs

During the first stage the front-end of the SUV was scanned and reconstruction of CAD surface models was performed (reverse engineering). The obtained geometrical model of the vehicle was further equipped with the frontal protection system, basing on the precise documentation (Fig. 2).

Fig. 2

The stages for FPS numerical tests: 3D scanning (left), FE model with FPS included (right)

The steel FPS was made from DIN 1.4301 steel alloy (AISI 304). A non-linear model of DIN 1.4301 steel alloy was implemented based on the 094_Simplified Johnson-Cook material model from the LS-DYNA database [10]. The material is characterized by the following physical parameters (Table 1).

Table 1

Physical properties of DIN 1.4301 steel [11]

Material density | 7900 kg/m3

---|---

Young's modulus | 200 GPa

Poisson's ratio | 0.3

A | 310 MPa

B | 1000 MPa

n | 0.65

c | 0.07

As a composite there was fiberglass chosen, but this material has a disadvantage—after the bursting sharp ends arise which can be dangerous to pedestrian in a collision. However, fiberglass has a high flexibility so it does not break at high angles of flexion, this advantage may have a positive impact on the health of pedestrian [12]. The reasons of choosing this kind of material were especially the high ratio of strength to density and the price which is about 10 time less than the price of carbon fibre [13]. Also, the authors currently lead research concerning fiberglass FPS structure coated with polyurethane which would prevent sharp edges of fiberglass to wound pedestrians.

As a worst case scenario chosen for boundary condition bumper and bonnet were fully constrained. The explicit Ls-Dyna finite element code was applied as a solver [14–16]. The material which was chosen to design FPS was a plain wave fiberglass S-2 Glass/SC-15, the material properties are shown in Table 2 (Fig. 3).

FPS was impacted by lower legform at 40 km/h. The contours of effective strain of fiberglass versus steel FPS at 38 ms after impact is depicted in Fig. 3.

Fig. 3

Contours of effective plastic strain [.] for steel (left) and fibreglass (right) FPS

During this simulation acceleration were measured at the upper end of the tibia (Fig. 4). In the case of fiberglass FPS maximum measured value of acceleration was 177.7g and for steel FPS measured value of acceleration was 300g.

Fig. 4

Acceleration measured at the upper end of the tibia

Also dynamic knee shearing displacement was measured. The highest value of it is equal to 2.7 mm for both fiberglass and steel FPS which is within the current limits (Fig. 5).

Fig. 5

Dynamic knee shearing displacement (FPS type 1)

The change of the dynamic knee bending angle is shown in Fig. 6. Maximum angle is 20.5° for fiberglass FPS and 17.5° for steel FPS. The limiting angle of 21° was not exceed in this test by any of the tested FPS (Fig. 6).

Fig. 6

Dynamic knee bending angle (FPS type 1)

## 3 Conclusions

Due to the large impact of pedestrian safety FPS must be correctly tested according to EC 78/2009 using leg and head impactors. In the article two variants of the same FPS design were tested—steel versus fiberglass. The fiberglass composite is increasingly used in automotive industry due to its low mass density and high strength. Thanks to that, FPS made of fiberglass may efficiently protect front elements of vehicle provided it is coated with an elastic material to prevent it from wounding pedestrian's body. Additionally, fiberglass flexibility can reduce injuries sustained by a pedestrian during an accident as evidenced by the results obtained during the impact legform to FPS. In this study all measured values are consistent with the EC 78/2009 unlike the steel design. The fiberglass FPS measured acceleration is about 1.7 times lower than in the case of the steel FPS. Further measured parameters are comparable which indicates the fiberglass S-2 Glass/SC-15 material may be used for FPS design.

# Computer Simulations for Head Injuries Verification After Impact

Mariusz Ptak1  , Paweł Kaczyński1  , Fabio Fernandes2  and Ricardo Alves de Sousa2

(1)

Department of Machine Design and Research, Wrocław University of Technology, Lukasiewicza 7/9, 50-371 Wroclaw, Poland

(2)

TEMA: Centre for Mechanical Technology and Automation, Department of Mechanical Engineering, University of Aveiro, Campus de Santiago, 3810-193 Aveiro, Portugal

Mariusz Ptak (Corresponding author)

Email: mariusz.ptak@pwr.edu.pl

Paweł Kaczyński

Email: pawel.kaczynski@pwr.edu.pl

Fabio Fernandes

Email: fabiofernandes@ua.pt

Ricardo Alves de Sousa

Email: rsousa@ua.pt

Abstract

The paper describes an experimental and numerical approach to head injury verification occurring in transportation accidents. Current trends in pedestrian, cyclist and motorcyclist safety are presented and some state-of-the-art techniques are included to mitigate injuries, which occur when an external force traumatically damages the brain. Finally, a finite element analysis was conducted to assess the safety performance of a commercial motorcycle helmet.

Keywords

Finite element head modelingImpactInjuryHelmetSimulationBiomechanics

## 1 Introduction

Computer simulations have been developing concurrently with the rapid growth of advanced computers. Currently, their contribution to the car designing and safety devices process is vital. When the Finite Element Method (FEM)—the technique used to determine the approximated solution for a partial differential equations on a defined domain—was started to be used by appropriate software, the complexities of modelling, including safety issues, could be addressed [1, 2]. Figure 1 depicts main approach to enhance pedestrian and cyclist safety.

Fig. 1

Pedestrian and cyclist issues involved in safety enhancement

Euro NCAP (New Car Assessment Programme) pedestrian protection ratings released in 1997 were also a trigger for a fruitful start of virtual tests. Nowadays, numerical simulations constitute the basis for the Computer-Aided Engineering (CAE) [3–7]. The excessive development of computation power and the expansion of FEM and MultiBody (MB) enabled researchers to widen the possibilities and applications to include car to vulnerable road user collisions.

The impact of a vehicle with a pedestrian has already been thoroughly studied and described in several publications, mainly through tests on human cadavers [8–10] and increasingly popular testing on pedestrian dummies, carried out mainly in Japanese centers [11, 12]. The pedestrian and cyclist side impact test is the most commonly performed test since, according to Yang and Jarret [13, 14], it accounts for approximately 80% of pedestrian accidents, who are most often hit while crossing the road [15].

Ravani [16], Keaser [17], and later Ishikawa [18] and Mizuno and Kajzer [19] addressed an issue known mainly from vehicle-to-vehicle collisions, [20], namely, that of the compatibility between vehicles and pedestrians. They stressed the influence of the geometry of mono-box vehicles on life-threatening injuries to the head, chest and abdomen. In the case of mono-box vehicles, injuries to these parts of the body are three times more frequent in comparison to compact vehicles with a clearly defined bonnet line (Fig. 2).

Fig. 2

Head-to-bonnet impact of a pedestrian in 100 ms after SUV-to-pedestrian accident at 40 km/h

The head impacts are the most dangerous types of accidents and traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a major cause of death and disability worldwide, especially in children and young adults. Worldwide, an estimated 10 million people are affected annually by traumatic brain injury (TBI) [21]. FE brain models have been used as an effective tool for the investigation of traumatic brain injuries. One of the most advanced head models is of Global Human Body Models Consortium (GHBMC) depicted in Fig. 3.

Fig. 3

Head and its section of 50th percentile male GHBMC model based on [22]

## 2 Experimental Helmet Tests

Nowadays, to create a customize helmet some 3D scanning equipment is used. The authors use Leica P20, where interferometry is realized by Waveform Digitizing technology (WFD)—the processor calculates distance as the time between reflected laser signal and referent signal. The precision of 3D point position is subjected to distance of measurements. The cloud of points obtained from 3D scanning, which is to be converted as a scull base to meet the ergonomics aspects, is depicted in Fig. 4.

Fig. 4

Customised helmet design—initial 3D head scanning with Leica P20 system

A numerical test allows conducting simulation without destruction of tested objects. This method however has some limitations, especially in case of new materials testing. EN960 standards requires preconditioning of materials, like: UV exposure, spraying with water, heating and cooling cycles. The creation of reliable material models taking this conditions into consideration would require expensive material tests (both static and dynamic). In this case testing of helmets is cheaper and faster using real head impactors (Fig. 5).

Fig. 5

EN960 magnesium headform type 575 for helmet testing (left) secured with attached helmet in free-fall test rig (right)

The depicted in Fig. 5. head impactor for helmet testing is fully compatible with the EN960:2007 standard. First stage of production was focused on creating 3D computer-aided digital models in order to take outer shape into consideration. In the second stage model were casted from magnesium alloy. The main features of headform are as follows:

  * resonance frequency >2000 Hz,

  * made of 100% magnesium alloy,

  * durable single-piece part,

  * sizes available: 495, 535, 575

The headform impactor is equipped with modular SLICE NANO standalone data acquisition system, which complies with ISO 6487 standard, SAE J211 recommended practices, as well as NHTSA and FAA requirements. It is lightweight and small recording system. Described measuring set allows for testing of various helmets, as:

  * hang gliding and paragliding (EN966),

  * equestrian sport (EN 14572),

  * high performance industrial helmets (EN 14052),

  * fire fighting in buildings and other structures (EN 443),

  * ski, snowboard (EN 1077), bicycle, skateboarders and roller skates users (EN 1078),

  * kids protective helmets (EN 1080),

## 3 Finite Element Approach for Motorcyclist Helmet Testing

The most common causes of TBI is transportation accidents, construction, and sports. Overall, motor bikes are major causes, increasing in significance in developing countries [23]. To prevent head injuries during an accident some energy-absorbing materials are used. Figure 6 shows the FE helmet model developed, which includes the shell and the dual-density energy absorbing liner composed by three different parts: the main padding that involves the entire cranium with the exception of temporal region, the forehead padding insert and the lateral padding (positioned in the temporal region). The different meshes characteristics are shown in the Fig. 2. The lateral liners are made of Expanded Polystyrene (EPS) foam with density of 90 kg/m3 and the remaining with 65 kg/m3 density. Thickness values vary from 10 to 50 mm, being inversely proportional to the density. The outer shell made of Acrylonitrile-butadiene-styrene (ABS) has a thickness of 3 mm. In this study, the effects of the comfort liner, the retention system (chin strap) and the chin pad were not considered.

Fig. 6

Finite Element Helmet Model—a cut view from the sagittal plane

According to ECE R22.05 regulation it is used a 5.6 kg headform (M size). The FE headform model used in the simulations is described in [24] and its inertial characteristics are given in Table 1.

Table 1

Headform | Rigid quadrangular shell | R3D4 | 1346 | 1348

Anvil | 1 | 4

In order to simulate the interfaces between the anvil and the helmet's shell, a surface-to-surface type of contact with a friction coefficient of 0.4 was used. The same type of contact but with a friction coefficient of 0.5 was used to model the interaction between the shell and the liner and between the headform and the liner. Also, a "tie" type contact was used to simulate the tie between the different parts of the liner (glued parts). The tie was also used to fully constrain the helmet's chin guard relatively to the main shell.

According to the ECE R22.05 standard, the helmet-headform system is dropped, without any restriction, against an anvil with velocity of 7.5 m/s. The simulated impacts were always against flat anvils only, which is enough for a first stage of the model validation. The flat anvil was fixed (fully constrained) and an impact velocity of 7.5 m/s was prescribed to the model. Figure 7 shows the impact configurations according to the ECE R22.05 standard, the B, P, R and X points.

In overall, there is a good agreement between experiments and simulations for all four points. The differences between experimental and numerical results may be explained by the adoption of a simplified numerical model regarding the number of helmet components modelled. For example, the helmet impacted area at point X is a zone that has several parts that were not modelled, since the visor locking system, the chin strap, the fixation system between the two parts of the shell and the comfort padding that has a considerable thickness at this region. Despite some differences between experimental and numerical impact results, the numerical model was considered adequate enough for a preliminary study on linear and oblique impacts with motorcycle helmets.

## 4 Summary

The main goal of the following paper is to present the great potential of using computer aided engineering in order to asset brain injury level. The paper describes the experimental and numerical approach to head injury verification occurring in transportation accidents. Additionally, a finite element analysis of helmet impacts were performed in order to validate the developed commercial motorcycle helmet model. Simulation results are in a good agreement with experimental data from energy absorption tests demanded by ECE R22.05 standard.
